chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, when a need of his brother comes to a believer, and it does not happen to be in his presence, his heart becomes concerned with it; therefore, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will enter him into Paradise due to his concern for it.

key_terms.فَيَهْتَمُّ بِهَا قَلْبُهُ: His heart becomes concerned with it
key_terms.لَتَرِدُ عَلَيْهِ الْحَاجَةُ: A need comes to him / is referred to him

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for a believer who feels concerned about a brother's need even if he cannot fulfill it immediately?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) to emphasize that the spiritual weight of *hamm* (sincere concern) is valued by Allah as highly as the physical act of fulfillment itself. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the internal state of the heart (*batin*) complementing outward action (*zahir*), suggesting that genuine empathy for a brother's plight is a direct path to Paradise, even if logistical constraints prevent immediate assistance.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from uhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Ju’fy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Momin to whom is referred to a need of his brother, so it does not happen to be in his presence, but he intends it in his heart, so Allahazwj Blessed and High would Enter him into the Paradise due to his intending for it’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma’il ibn Bazi’ from Salih ibn ‘Aqabah from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Ju’fi from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“A believer may find his brother (in belief) needy in a certain matter that is not available to him and he intends in his heart to meet such need, Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, admits him in paradise just because of his intention.”
